To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the research in the collaboration systems domain at the ICE conferences advanced from tools & technology, via methods and processes, to principles and rationale.

the research community of ICE is moving from a technology focus to a process focus in collaboration system design, and that the research community is moving from a focus on the design of collaboration systems, to a focus on the use of collaboration systems, and to the design of collaboration system use, which can be seen in the evolution of the conference track titles from “collaboration tools & technology” to “collaboration methods” and to “collaborative systems”.

collaboration systems research is a key enabler of engineering productivity, and that this is achieved by a combination of tools and technology, methods and processes and working and organising principles.

the development and application of systems for engineering collaboration.
how engineers work together, how to make them more efficient and effective in their collaboration and how to make their collaboration more rewarding.
the development of collaboration systems for engineering.

the research on collaboration systems is in line with the general trend of the ICE conference to advance the understanding of the engineering enterprise.
the track collaboration systems is the right track for ICE.
collaboration systems is a mature research topic at the ICE conference, with a track record in research results, methodologies, and systems approaches.

the research at the ICE community has moved from the description of tools to the understanding of the rationale and the principles of engineering collaboration systems.
